title: Connected degree-18 zero-neighborhood-excess exclusion attempt

status_update.current: The q1,E_A=0 slice is now excluded by a separate independently accepted proof. Every zero-A-excess degree18 root requires q>=2 and x>=140; higher q remains open. The original ready claims below retain their historical review state.

author: Main, working alone at the user's request
result: Not excluded. Necessary reductions and an exact first-surviving-slice core theorem, not a nonexistence proof.
novelty: No novelty claim or external literature review. Existing literature premises are retained as recorded in the cited repository sources.

scope.G: A simple order-43 graph with no K5 and no independent 5-set
scope.A: N_G(v), order 18, connected and K4/I5-free. A may contain independent 4-sets and in fact must contain one by R(4,4)=18.
scope.zero_excess: Every u in A has global degree 18. This is W_A=E_A=0, not the assertion that all of G is 18-regular.
scope.notation: a=e(A), q=85-a, x=e(A,B), b=e(B), epsilon_z=d_G(z)-18, W=sum_z epsilon_z, R_u=N_B(u), E_u=sum_{z adjacent u}epsilon_z. Here W denotes total graph excess only.

premise_ledger.used: Nonnegative epsilon, the identity x=136+2q+E_A, 0<=q<=35, and 144<=b<=160, on the recorded degree and census premises.
At every degree-18 root u: b_u=148+W/2-q_u-E_u and q_u+E_u<=W/2+4.

Independently accepted unavoidable independent-four anchor with all internal degrees at least 8 when q=1,E_A<=29. The present use has E_A=0 and does not rely on the separately pending parameter-landscape audit.
For nonadjacent degree-18 roots, common-neighbor overlap is 1..8, the two opposite mixed cells are (4,4)-free of order 18-overlap, and the common-nonneighbor cell is (5,3)-free.
Existing independent-four global signature accounting and its exceptional-core alternative. The new q=1 specialization tracks which signatures lie in A versus B and uses the common root v.

C136 denotes the user's reported closure of the whole x=136 case. The report is accepted as supplied, with its proof still pending checkout integration. Only conclusions explicitly marked conditional on C136 use it.

claims.scope: Every rooted graph in the scope above, with no q=1 assumption
conclusion: x=136+2q is even, b=148-q+W/2, and max(0,2q-8)<=W<=2q+24. Thus W<=94 and at least 19 vertices have degree 18.
Conditional on C136, q>=1 and x is in {138,140,...,206}. Without C136, retain q=0 as well.
If W=0, then q<=4. Conditional on C136, the all-18-regular subcase still has q in {1,2,3,4}, with x in {138,140,142,144}.
For u in A, E_u=sum_{y in R_u}epsilon_y. For every independent four I in A, sum_{u in I}E_u>=W. In particular E_u=0 for all u in A if and only if W=0.
proof: The original pivot and every A vertex have epsilon 0, so all excess lies in B. Substitute E_A=0 in the exact cross-count identity. Count total edges as 18+a+x+b=387+W/2 to get b=148-q+W/2. Substituting 144<=b<=160 gives 2q-8<=W<=2q+24. Nonnegative W and q<=35 give the stated range and W<=94. The 19 vertices {v} union A all have degree 18.
C136 deletes q=0 because E_A=0. At W=0 the lower bound 2q-8<=0 gives q<=4. These scalar facts do not assert realizability.

For u in A, its neighbors in {v} union A carry no excess, leaving exactly R_u in the formula for E_u. Every column C_y=N_A(y) meets every independent four I in A, or y together with I gives I5. Therefore sum_{u in I}E_u=sum_{y in B}epsilon_y*|C_y intersect I|>=sum_{y in B}epsilon_y=W. Such an I exists because A is K4-free of order 18 and R(4,4)=18. If all the E_u vanish then W=0, and the converse is immediate from nonnegative excess.

claims.scope: Every independent four I in A in the full zero-excess branch
dependencies: global degree 18 at every member of I
claims.notation: s=sum_{i in I}d_A(i), eta=32-s. For j=1..4, a_j and b_j count vertices in A-I and B respectively having exactly j neighbors in I.
conclusion: At eta=0 there are no singleton signatures in A-I and no triple or quadruple signatures in B. All four B singleton classes are triangles of order 3.
If I has d_A(i)=8 for all i, each I vertex occurs in exactly 6 of the B double signatures.
proof: No vertex outside I has empty signature, by I5-freeness. A global exact singleton class is a clique: two nonadjacent members together with the other 3 roots give I5. Its size is at most 3, since 4 clique members together with its root give K5. Thus the total global singleton count a_1+b_1 is at most 12.

Each I vertex has B-degree 17-d_A(i). Consequently e(I,B)=68-s=36+eta. Counting the 24 B vertices gives b_1+b_2+b_3+b_4=24 and -b_1+b_3+2*b_4=eta-12. In particular eta=12-b_1+b_3+2*b_4>=0, since b_1<=12. Combining b_1=12-eta+b_3+2*b_4 with a_1+b_1<=12 gives the first inequality.
Counting the 14 vertices of A-I and their s incidences gives a_1+a_2+a_3+a_4=14 and -a_1+a_3+2*a_4=s-28=4-eta, proving the exact identity.

At eta=0 the nonnegative terms a_1,b_3,b_4 vanish, and b_1=12. Each B singleton class attains its global cap 3 and hence is a triangle. If all four internal degrees are 8, each corresponding B row has size 9, consisting of its 3 singleton vertices and 6 double signatures.

claims.scope: The q=1, E_A=0 slice, equivalently a=84 and x=138
conclusion: An independent four I in A exists with all four d_A(i)=8. It 2-dominates A-I: every vertex of A-I has at least 2 neighbors in I.

Relative to I the B signatures are exactly 12 singletons, 3 of each type, and 12 doubles, with 6 doubles incident to each root. Up to j=1,2,3,4 the A-I signature counts are exactly (0,10,4,0), (0,11,2,1), or (0,12,0,2). In all cases e(A-I)=52.

Exactly one of the following holds: (i) two members of I have overlap 3..6, yielding opposite actual (4,4)-free mixed cells of orders 12..15; (ii) every pair in I has overlap 7, and the exact exceptional allocation described in the next claim holds.
proof: The reviewed q=1 anchor theorem applies because E_A=0<=29. It supplies I with all d_A(i)>=8. The defect inequality in the preceding claim forces s<=32, so all four degrees equal 8 and eta=0. All the zero-defect conclusions follow.

Set t=a_4. The equations a_1=0, a_2+a_3+a_4=14 and 2*a_2+3*a_3+4*a_4=32 give a_3=4-2*t and a_2=10+t. Nonnegativity gives t in {0,1,2}. Deleting the independent anchor removes exactly s=32 edges, so e(A-I)=84-32=52.

Globally outside I, include v, whose signature is all four. The counts are n_1=12, n_2=22+t, n_3=4-2*t, n_4=1+t. Counting pairs of I neighbors of each external vertex gives the sum of the 6 pair overlaps as n_2+3*n_3+6*n_4=40+t. If every overlap is at least 7, the sum is at least 42, forcing t=2 and every overlap exactly 7. Otherwise some pair has overlap at most 6.

For any pair i,j in I, their 8-element A neighborhoods lie inside the same 14-element set A-I, so they have at least 2 common A neighbors. The pivot v is an additional common neighbor outside A. Thus every global pair overlap is at least 3. The mixed-cell sizes and types now follow from the reviewed nonadjacent-root cell theorem. No density or zero-neighborhood-excess condition is imposed on the re-rooted pair without proof.

dependencies: degree sums at the 4 anchor vertices
claims.notation: For a pair ij of I={1,2,3,4}, let alpha_ij count its exact double signatures in A-I, and beta_ij those in B. Order the 3 opposite-pair matchings as (12,34),(13,24),(14,23).
conclusion: All singleton classes lie in B and have size 3. All triple classes are empty. The all-four class is {v,p,q}, where p,q are in A and all 3 vertices have degree 18. Its induced graph is P3 centered at v or K3.

alpha_ij+beta_ij=4 for every pair, and alpha and beta separately have equal counts on opposite pairs. Writing the 3 beta matching counts as (r,s,t), they are integers in 0..4 with r+s+t=6, and the alpha matching counts are (4-r,4-s,4-t).
Up to relabelling I, the 5 beta triples are (0,2,4), (0,3,3), (1,1,4), (1,2,3), (2,2,2). These are count allocations, not 5 graph isomorphism types or certified feasible graphs.
proof: Alternative (ii) has t=a_4=2 in the preceding notation. Thus the 2 internal all-four vertices together with v give the entire global all-four class, and there are no triples. The two internal vertices are adjacent to v and all have degree 18 by the original zero-excess assumption. Their mutual adjacency is the only undecided edge within this 3-set, giving P3 or K3.
For each pair of anchor roots, the 3 all-four vertices contribute 3 to its overlap 7, leaving exactly 4 vertices in its exact double class. Hence alpha_ij+beta_ij=4.

Each anchor root has B-degree 9 and 3 B singleton neighbors, giving beta degree sum 6 at every root. Its A-degree is 8, of which 2 goes to p,q, giving alpha degree sum 6 as well. For 6 pair counts on 4 labels with all 4 row sums equal, subtracting row equations gives equality on opposite pairs. Their 3 matching counts sum to 6. Nonnegativity of alpha and beta bounds each beta matching count by 4. The sorted integer triples with sum 6 and entries between 0 and 4 are precisely the displayed 5. Permutations of anchor labels realize all permutations of the 3 opposite-pair matchings, so sorting loses no count orbit.

failed_exclusion_routes.route: Identify zero A-excess with the equality frontier
failed_exclusion_routes.obstruction: The exact identity is x=136+2q. Zero excess fixes the parity, not q. C136 removes q=0 only.

failed_exclusion_routes.route: Propagate zero neighborhood excess through all neighbors
failed_exclusion_routes.obstruction: All neighbors have degree 18, but their own neighborhood excess can be positive. In fact for any independent four I in A, sum_I E_u>=W, so zero at all 18 neighbors would force the strictly stronger W=0 case.

failed_exclusion_routes.route: Obtain a scalar contradiction from the q=1 saturated anchor
failed_exclusion_routes.obstruction: All 3 signature profiles have explicit nonnegative count assignments satisfying the 4 anchor row sums and the pair-overlap bounds. All 5 exceptional allocations also satisfy these equations. These assignments do not set edges between external vertices and are not Ramsey constructions.

failed_exclusion_routes.route: Transfer the reported x136 closure wholesale to q=1
failed_exclusion_routes.obstruction: The q=1 anchor has the same saturated B signature pattern, but a=84 and e(A-I)=52, rather than a=85 and e(A-I)=53. The unintegrated closure proof cannot be assumed to survive losing this edge.

failed_exclusion_routes.route: Use connectedness to delete the remaining q>1 slices
failed_exclusion_routes.obstruction: No such implication was proved. Connectedness is already automatic for q<=16 by the reviewed connectivity threshold. The present deductions deliberately do not claim coverage by the q=1 core theorem for q=2..35.

remaining_obstruction.q1: Must exclude all actual completions of the low-overlap pair branch and all actual completions of the 5 exceptional count allocations. External-vertex adjacencies in A-I, B, and the cross matrix are not determined by signature counts.
remaining_obstruction.all_q: Conditional on the supplied x136 closure, q=1..35 remains in the zero-excess branch until further structural exclusion. The q=1 refinement does not cover q>=2.
remaining_obstruction.next_mathematical_target: Study compatibility of the actual (4,4) mixed cells of orders 12..15 in the low-overlap branch. In the exceptional branch retain the degree-18 P3/K3 all-four core and all 5 opposite-pair allocations. Any proof must also handle q>=2 rather than declaring the whole branch closed.

verification.type: Author self-audit of proofs and exact scalar arithmetic, not independent review
verification.method: Compare row sums with pair-overlap counts and global singleton capacity, then evaluate the finite integer identities. Reproducer and source hashes retained in the dated report.
verification.result: PASS: 3 internal signature profiles, 5 exceptional count orbits, 28 labelled regular B-double assignments, 3 explicit count-only witnesses, 602 budget cells, and 19 labelled exceptional allocations.
verification.limits: No graph search or graph realizability check. No solver, Lean, downloads, subagents, or accepted-status changes. No branch is excluded.
